x: Congratulations to Dave Ansell, our Captain, on his selection for the British team at the Maccabia Games in Tel-a-Viv. He was 7th in the long jump, 6th in the triple jump and gained a medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay.

D.Ansell showed good early season form in the long jump, with four jumps over 20 ft; his best, 20'6½" gained him second place. Dave Ansell(19'8") was beaten on the last jump by one inch for second place, and finished third, four inches behind the winner. Coleman collected a point here for his fourth place and a further two in the shot, which was won by Rasey, our 3rd(!) claim member from Southgate and Barnet.

There were two races over 440 yds, Charlie Jones being second (52 4) in the first one and Alan Jackson winning the second in 52 6 Dave Ansell won the 100 yds in 10 8s. and the long jump with 20'7". The match resulted in a win for Victoria Park with 104 pts.

The following performances were recorded:- Compiled by D.

Belgravians did quite well at this meeting with Dave Ansell beating 22 ft. in his first long jump of the season and Charlie Jones lowering his previous best quarter time by 0.9s., also in his first attempt this season.

…), Derek McCorquindale, in his first outing for Belgrave, showed his class and won the shot with 49'0¼" and our Captain Dave Ansell took second place in the long jump with 21'4½" and, deputising for Norman Caves, 5th in the triple jump at 42'3½" (a personal best).…

Dave Ansell, runner up in the Sward Trophy a few days earlier could only manage 4th place this time with a similar distance! Jim McGrath, our new member from Northern Ireland who seems to be another Mal Ash, jumped a most creditable 21'0" to finish 5th.
Jim McGrath showed his versatility by adding the discus to his list of events, and continued his battle of the "half-inch" with Dave Ansell in the long jump.

Both Jim and Dave Ansell, who was fourth, recorded 20'3", the wind accounting for a good two feet. Dave went on to a fourth place in the triple jump while Jim completed a "Mal Ash" type performance by finishing third in the pole vault, narrowly failing at 12'0", an excellent days work.

In the Middlesex Championships at Enfield Dave Ansell was once more amongst the leading long jumpers and finished second with 21'5¼". John Davies, holder of the mile title, was unable to compete owing to other commitments.
The field events boys were out in force and both Percy Porter and Dave Ansell won their respective events - the hammer, with 158'10½", and the long-jump with a leap of 20'5½".

Jim's long-jump twin Dave Ansell did his duty with a winning jump of 20feet 10½inches. Alan Black was a close runner-up in the 1500 metres s/chase to Barry Collins (Surrey) who is the country's leading junior performer at this event.

Dereck McCorquindale won the shot with a putt of 46ft 4½ins, whilest Dave Ansell secured third place in the long-jump with 21'4¾". In a very close 100 yds finish Sylvan Deane was 4th in 10.5 secs; and to complete the picture Eric Smith was sixth in the 2 mile walk.
Dave Ansell has had quite a good season, attaining a place in the Middlesex Championships and winning the Maccabi European Championship with 22ft odd.
An inch meant the difference between 1st and 2nd place in the Long Jump, where Dave Ansell (21'10") and Jim McGrath were squeezed out of their winner's medals.

Dave Ansell, still not completely free from injury, finished third in the long jump with a plus 21 feet leap. Alan Black and Clive Shippen ran in the 3,000 metres steeplechase, but with 3 laps to go Alan dropped out when in 2nd place, leaving Clive to finish third in 9-57.0.

His victory in the long jump was no surprise, for with the absence of his "twin", Dave Ansell, Jim's only serious rival was Norman Caves; although young Derek Wade gave them both a scare by recording six valid jumps between 18'3½" and 18'10".
Coach Dave Ansell achieved a lifetime best in the shot and with his generous handicap mark of 15'3" took 1st prize from Tony Brooks and John Kelly.

A poor entry of only eight competitors for the Shot Putt handicap but nevertheless an enjoyable competition won by Lyle Moar with a personal best and Dave Ansell 2nd with a special handicap for taking part in his best suit.

The 'Southern' Long Jump was one of the closest events at this meeting and was a triumph for Dave Ansell.
